name: Clay Craft India Limited
summary: Established ceramic franchise with positive adjusted cash conversion. Primary IPO monitoring supports a funded project bridge; conditional base return is 20.77% at the dated ₹167 close. Moderate capital efficiency, commissioning risk and concentrated trading breadth prevent treating the valuation allowance as certain.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Watchlist with favorable conditional valuation, not a proven compounder or an automatic buy. Clay Craft has an established ceramic franchise and cash-positive operations, while the new porcelain plant is a substantial execution and capital-return test. The official June monitoring report now supports a real IPO/bridge-finance reconciliation, replacing the earlier arbitrary starting cash/debt assumptions. At the dated ₹167 close, the funded base yields 20.77% annually against a 15% hurdle; simultaneous margin and multiple misses can erase that allowance. Serious stress still risks permanent capital loss.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026. NSE Emerge CLAYCRAFT, ISIN INE1QGM01024, listed 24 June 2026. Official 19 October SM close ₹167, 20,570,280 shares and ₹343.52 crore equity value; not a live executable quote. The board lot is 600 shares, costing ₹100,200. FY21–23 statutory standalone and FY24 standalone/FY25–26 restated consolidated histories are separated. The investor horizon is five years to 19 October 2031, with annual FY27–31 and a fiscal stub from March balances plus explicit IPO events. The 15% equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh reference are analytical conventions. All four gates are Conditional rather than failed; model outputs do not establish current October cash or sanctioned future lending.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.56; GQS 5.35; conditional IAS 6.49. R/D/P/L 8/5/6/7. All canonical factors have medium-confidence evidence; no missing-factor reweighting or critical gate override. REV 4 uses the less pandemic-distorted three-year window; CAP 5 does not transfer mature ROCE to uncommissioned capacity. The funding bridge supports BAL 6 and a numerical R instead of a blanket evidence hold. The full audit retains weights and contributions. Moving CAP or BAL by one point changes BQS by 0.12 or 0.08, and changing R by one point changes IAS by 0.35; small score differences should not be overinterpreted.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Clay Craft manufactures ceramic tableware for household, hospitality, gifting and institutional customers under its own Clay Craft/JCPL brands and customer designs. Distributors and retailers are important routes to market, supported by design and a wide SKU range. Existing 6,000 MT capacity is distinct from the prospective 4,000 MT hard-porcelain line, whose product characteristics and customer qualification differ. Ekling Ji’s merger predominantly transferred investments/cash and family ownership, not a large acquired operating business. Crown Craft was equity accounted until its holding fell from 27.93% to 19.67% in July 2025; it does not justify adding its gross sales to Clay Craft.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Approximately 132 distributors, 5,700 SKUs, internal design and established brands support moderate differentiation, not unlimited pricing power. Suppliers are concentrated: the top three represent 52.28% and top ten 78.86% of FY26 purchases. Distribution and supply contracts are not exclusive. September’s announced anti-dumping sunset review is only an initiation, not a final extension or guaranteed protection. La Opala is a useful substitute-tableware comparator with opal/crystal glass technology and 32,000 MT capacity, but a different mix and investment base. FY26 revenue ₹309.06 crore, pre-exception core EBITDA ₹115.73 crore, exceptional cost ₹1.79 crore, PAT ₹92.30 crore and CFO ₹67.61 crore show why core operations, investment income and cash must be separated. Its higher margin or reported operating-return definition is not transplanted into Clay Craft.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY21–26 revenue is ₹74.1025/₹114.5416/₹145.3083/₹145.4255/₹151.9422/₹179.8867 crore. Five-year CAGR is 19.41%, but starts in a pandemic trough; the preferred three-year CAGR is 7.38% and FY23–24 was almost flat. Latest growth is 18.39%, encouraging but insufficient to erase the plateau. PAT of ₹19.948 crore in FY23 fell to ₹13.502 crore in FY24, then recovered to ₹20.7574/₹27.0149 crore. The historical statutory/restated scope difference is explicit. FY26 exports are only ₹0.2933 crore, so a premium export-led porcelain ramp is a prospective execution claim, not a current revenue engine.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The ₹126.4168 crore project includes GST and adds 4,000 MT to existing 6,000 MT nameplate capacity. Net IPO proceeds are ₹97.0188 crore after estimated ₹13.0884 crore issue costs; ₹97 crore is allocated to the plant, leaving an approximately ₹29.42 crore project funding need before working capital. The June monitor verifies ₹58.45 crore project utilization: ₹38.68 crore direct vendor payments and ₹19.77 crore repayment of the pre-IPO FD overdraft. Gross unspent IPO cash is ₹41.18 crore, including ₹38.55 crore monitored project cash and ₹2.63 crore public-issue cash, not a second inflow. The September 80%+ utilization wording combines purchase orders and invoices and is not substituted for paid cash. February 2027 commissioning and ₹150–160 crore optimal annual sales are management targets. Base FY27 new-line utilization is only 1% of full-year capacity, then 35/55/70/80%; the future ramp is an assumption, not contracted sales.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Family economics are material and disclosed. FY26 Sharp Minchem purchases were ₹14.3762 crore; remuneration to Rajesh, Bharat and Deepak was ₹2.0282/₹1.7201/₹1.7201 crore. These amounts require minority scrutiny but do not themselves establish abuse. Estimated IPO costs consume 11.89% of gross funds. The merger altered ownership and investment assets; it is not treated as a large operating acquisition or automatic misconduct.

The June prospectus identifies Complaint Case 42474/2025 against the company and MD/promoter Vikas Agarwal before CMM/ACMM Jaipur Metro HQ II, concerning customs classification of imported calcium phosphate. It reports pending cognizance/process/service, with a then-scheduled 30 July 2026 hearing; the current disposition was not established in reviewed sources. Separately, CESTAT’s 27 April 2026 order upheld differential duty of approximately ₹62.73 lakh and an equivalent penalty; the company filed a Rajasthan High Court appeal/stay application on 2 June, disclosed as pending registration. The prospectus states ₹125.47 lakh plus possible interest for the prosecution-related matter and ₹125.46 lakh for duty/penalty. These concern the same underlying classification exposure and are not added twice. An adverse duty adjudication is not a criminal conviction, and no later outcome is invented.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Three-year reported CFO/PAT is 1.29×, but interest is classified in financing. Deducting that interest and the FY25 merger-reserve/tax adjustments reduces the diagnostic to about 1.05×, still positive. FY26 reported CFO ₹26.6449 crore less ₹6.7125 crore PPE/CWIP purchases is ₹19.9324 crore before financing interest and deposits, not fully distributable FCF. Core EBITDA excluding all other income is ₹41.8596 crore, 23.27% of operating revenue. Broad normalized ROIC is approximately 13.2%, around a reasoned 12–16% capital-cost range. The new plant’s terminal NOPAT/project-plus-WC proxy is only about 10.7%, so a mature reported ROCE does not prove excellent incremental returns.

Opening usable current cash is ₹0.1318 crore. ₹51.277 crore FDs and ₹1.1351 crore margin deposits are kept separate from ₹49.9774 crore borrowings. The model settles current gratuity/leave ₹1.6852 crore once, while normal bonus ₹1.7265 crore and ₹10.814 crore statutory/salary/director/expense/customer dues remain in WC. Advance tax/TDS ₹9.0024 crore exceeds the ₹8.7283 crore current provision: the net ₹0.2741 crore asset is recovered once by assumption, with nonrecovery tested, not charged as a payable. Noncurrent employee ₹4.474 crore, DTL ₹4.5275 crore and security deposits ₹0.0153 crore remain terminal claims. GST compensation-cess ₹1.393 crore and old accrued interest ₹1.731 crore are excluded from ordinary WC/free cash until recovered.

The bank-return note shows ₹17.3077 crore book receivables versus ₹11.0213 crore submitted to the bank. Management states reconciliation; no independent detailed bridge was supplied. The submitted figure is lower, not evidence of an inflated borrowing base. Inventory and collection monitoring remain important, but the difference is not used to allege fraud or invalidate every financial factor.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹167, current-share FY26 P/E is approximately 12.72×. Historical earnings precede deployment of new IPO capital, so this is a cross-check rather than a forward return forecast. The annual model uses actual March balances, the net IPO reserve, the separately disclosed bridge draw/repayment, full plant cash cost and operating WC. New draws incur half-year interest; excess-cash repayments occur at year-end. Positive-profit cash tax is 25.168%, with current tax assets/employee claims handled separately. No unspent project reserve can repay unrelated debt automatically.

Bear/base/bull prices are ₹170.32/₹428.97/₹656.48 and annualized returns 0.39%/20.77%/31.49%; peak debt, including temporary bridge OD, is ₹83.20/₹70.01/₹70.01 crore. The base reaches about ₹350.05 crore annual revenue at terminal, using 88% legacy and 80% new-line utilization with 2% annual price/mix growth and 23% margins. Its 12%/15%/18% hurdle entries are ₹243.41/₹213.27/₹187.51, assumption-dependent outputs rather than buy limits. At base operations an 8× exit gives 16.0%; a three-point margin reduction at 10× gives 16.5%; both together give 11.7%. The full grid reruns funding, not only terminal arithmetic.

A 20% project overrun yields 19.90% with ₹84.39 crore peak debt; a one-year delayed new-line ramp yields 19.44%. Zero FD cash interest gives 20.42%; no reimbursement of March prepaid IPO costs gives 20.74%. March Manda CWIP/capital-advance credit, tax nonrecovery, old-interest/cess recovery, customs/guarantee stresses and a cash-plus-shares 20% equity case are separately linked. All are conditional sensitivities, not evidence that bank headroom or asset recovery is available.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Ordinary bear assumptions reduce legacy utilization and new-line ramp, use 19% legacy margin, 42% WC, a 15% project overrun and 8× exit. Terminal price is ₹170.32, roughly preserving nominal entry value but yielding only 0.39% annually, with ₹83.20 crore peak debt. This is not a guaranteed price floor. Severe legacy demand loss, no new-line revenue, 13% margin, 48% WC, 30% cost overrun and a 20% inventory/receivable impairment produce zero common equity and ₹153.45 crore peak debt. Impairment risk is Moderate to High: existing operations, deposits and IPO equity support resilience, but specialist-plant recovery, bank renewal and cash conversion can fail together. Customs and guarantee calls are separately modeled stresses, not presumed adverse outcomes; ordinary booked obligations are not double charged.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged shares, 5×/10× require terminal equity of approximately ₹1,718/₹3,435 crore. At a 10× EBITDA multiple, 23% margin and zero net claims, that implies sales around ₹747/₹1,494 crore before considering dilution and funding. Legacy nameplate at FY26 realization plus management’s new-line midpoint supports roughly ₹374 crore before price growth and utilization discounts, far below those thresholds. The funded bull reaches ₹656.48, about 3.93× the ₹167 entry, not 5×. Material additional capacity, better economics or a longer horizon would be needed; none is assigned free capital or a success probability.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor separately: actual paid project invoices versus commitments; restricted IPO reserve and FD/OD release; February commissioning, product qualification and monthly utilization; inventory ageing, collections and bank-return reconciliation; operating margin excluding investment income; net employee/tax settlement and cess-credit recovery; related-party terms and court updates; and live trading breadth, spread and lot capacity. A one-year commissioning delay, new-line margin below 15% at meaningful utilization, or persistent WC above 40% of sales should prompt a model revision. These are analyst monitoring thresholds, not issuer guidance. Investor meetings alone are not new operating evidence.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Watchlist with favorable conditional valuation and moderate business quality. The old universal funding-data hold is no longer necessary because the primary monitor supplies a usable bridge; actual interim cash and commissioning remain uncertain, as for any forward model. The base return exceeds the hurdle without assuming principal recovery of pledged FDs, but combined operating and multiple misses do not. A purchase decision still requires position-specific risk, current execution conditions and evidence that the plant is becoming productive. No recommended portfolio weight or assurance of return is supplied.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Original final prospectus financial/claim notes, statutory P&L history, project objects, CARE monitoring and issuer updates form the record. Original monitor layout confirms ₹19.77 crore OD repayment, avoiding an OCR error. The source-specific old cash-flow history remains limited where scanned statutory reports do not provide a verified comparable series; three restated cash years are not mislabeled five. Secondary narrative and management targets do not replace primary cash evidence. All material ordinary dues, tax offsets, employee claims, tied deposits, interest timing and dilution are allocated once. Model assumptions and sensitivities remain separate from reported facts; no current court outcome, unrestricted FD release or committed new facility is fabricated.

limitations: The quote is an official 19 October close, not live execution data; lot granularity and exact exchange breadth/SME cautions constrain theoretical turnover capacity.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Conditional numeric scores at dated official price and stated position/model assumptions; not execution clearance.

liquidity.limits: Mean/median capacity is theoretical; live spread, depth, queue and actual buyer breadth matter. Lot is 20.04% of reference position.

GOV.reason: Family remuneration and procurement, sizeable IPO costs and a disclosed customs proceeding warrant scrutiny. Counterevidence is explicit transaction/claim disclosure, a primarily investment/cash merger and no established conviction or demonstrated severe minority abuse. Ordinary tax disputes and a one-time merger are not automatic integrity failures.

MOAT.reason: Established brands, design breadth, distribution and industrial know-how support differentiation. Contrary: concentrated raw-material suppliers, nonexclusive channels, competitive imports and new-product qualification limit pricing power. An anti-dumping review is not a permanent moat.

REV.reason: Available preferred three-year FY23–26 CAGR is 7.38%, mapping to 4 without adjustment. The 19.41% five-year rate begins in pandemic-affected FY21 and masks the FY23–24 plateau. Merger assets were predominantly investments/cash and the associate was equity accounted, supporting approximate parent operating comparability without pretending all old statutory profits were restated.

DUR.reason: Existing output is 82% of capacity and adjacent porcelain expansion has a specific funded project object, creating a tangible runway. Contrary: optimal sales are a management indication, not contracted demand; exports are currently small and customers must qualify new products.

CAP.reason: Broad normalized return on average equity-plus-debt-minus-free-cash is approximately 13.2%, around a 12–16% capital-cost range rather than clear excess return. The illustrative new-plant NOPAT/project-plus-WC return is about 10.7%. Existing cash generation is positive, but the new ₹126.42 crore facility cannot automatically inherit mature reported ROCE.

CASH.reason: Three-year reported CFO/PAT is 1.29×; after financing-classified interest and the FY25 merger reserve/tax adjustments it remains about 1.05×. All three reported years are cash-positive. Contrary: inventory and receivables grow, most deposits are collateral-bound, and reported CFO is not automatically distributable cash.

BAL.reason: March debt is ₹49.98 crore, with free current cash only ₹0.132 crore and ₹51.28 crore separately tracked FDs. Verified IPO proceeds and monitoring materially support the plant bridge; base peak debt including temporary OD is ₹70.01 crore. Bear/severe funding rises to ₹83.20/₹153.45 crore and requires continued banking access. No unrestricted deposit release or committed future facility is assumed.

EXEC.reason: Output increased from 4,092 MT in FY24 to 4,920 MT in FY26 and the monitor verifies actual vendor payments/OD repayment. Contrary: the new plant remains a commissioning target, August utilization language includes commitments, and the FY24 profit decline limits a smooth execution narrative.

EARN.reason: Recent core operating profit improves, but FY23–24 profit fell and investment/interest income contributes to reported PAT. The equity-method associate has limited revenue-scope effect; current shares dilute static historical EPS. New capacity must earn the cash raised, not merely expand reported assets.

R.reason: Funded base annualized return is 20.77%, 5.77 percentage points above the 15% hurdle, mapping mechanically to 8. Zero FD cash interest and no prepaid-IPO-cost reimbursement stay in the same R band. The model includes project cash, WC, tax, claims and new-draw interest; it does not use the old arbitrary October cash/debt assumptions.

D.reason: The ordinary bear preserves approximately nominal entry value at ₹170.32, but requires ₹83.20 crore peak debt; the combined severe demand, delay, cost-overrun and WC case eliminates common equity and needs ₹153.45 crore debt. Existing plants, cash generation, deposits and IPO equity support survival, but specialized-asset recovery and stress borrowing are not assured.

P.reason: The dated price broadly requires a fair execution case rather than extraordinary growth: 8× exit with base operations yields about 16.0%, and a three-point margin reduction at 10× yields 16.5%. Combining both reduces return to 11.7%, below hurdle. Thus the apparent valuation allowance is real but not robust to multiple simultaneous misses.

L.reason: The official 60-session mean/median gives 1.68 days at 5% participation, a starting 9. Reduce one point for the ₹100,200 lot (20.04% of reference position) and one for the exact active less-than-100-PAN breadth caution plus unavailable live depth. The exchange also flags SME not regularly traded; this does not erase 60 actual observed sessions or invent missing days.

financial_history.limitation: Older statutory values not restated to IPO basis; merger assets primarily investment/cash. Does not assume full comparability of PAT.

gates.reason: Disclosed related transactions and pending customs proceedings require source-attributed monitoring, not assumed criminal guilt or diversion. No demonstrated critical shareholder-abuse finding.

Restated financials, opening claim notes and original monitoring table support a bounded funded model. Bank-return differences and commitments-versus-cash wording remain explicit; no material universal reliability failure is established.

Actual IPO/OD deployment bridge materially resolves the former starting-point gap. Future draws, delayed-project cost and collateral release are assumptions rather than sanctioned finance; severe stress could require recapitalization.
Dated official trading and eligible SM series support limited capacity analysis. Active exchange breadth/SME cautions, lot size and missing live depth prevent execution assurance.

conventions: March balances are actual restated inputs. IPO net cash is added once, with ₹97 crore project reserve released only against modeled project cash spending. Unreleased reserve cannot automatically repay unrelated debt. June monitoring amounts reconcile gross proceeds approximately due to rounding; they are not extra inflows on top of IPO cash.

Project cost is ₹126.4168 crore including GST. Main reference conservatively assumes no credit for March Manda CWIP/capital advances whose precise project allocation is unverified; a ₹2.1684 crore credit is separately tested. Project cash includes the June funded advance and direct vendor spending, not an additional repayment charge. No uncertain input-tax recovery is assumed to shrink the project cash cost.

The pre-IPO FD overdraft is absent from March borrowings: disclosed June ₹20.03 crore draw and ₹19.77 crore repayment create a modeled ₹0.26 crore residual. Gross bridge cash flows are shown once. Temporary bridge interest assumes a quarter at 7.5%, and residual/new borrowing has half-year interest; ordinary repayments occur at year-end. Actual dates/utilization can differ.

The ₹0.5897 crore March prepaid IPO cost is assumed reimbursed within the total issue-cost budget, avoiding charging the same cost twice. A no-reimbursement sensitivity retains that source-allocation uncertainty. No full gross-IPO windfall is added to net proceeds.

Current tax is a net asset of ₹0.2741 crore after advance tax/TDS offsets, recovered once in FY27 by assumption; nonrecovery is tested. Current gratuity and leave ₹1.6852 crore settle once. Normal bonus, statutory, salary, director remuneration and expense payables remain in operating WC. Noncurrent employee liabilities, DTL and security deposits are retained at terminal, not blanket paid immediately.

All March FDs are separately ring-fenced in reference, despite short maturity; ₹1.1351 crore explicit margin deposits are never used. Future FD cash interest defaults to 80% of 5% accrual, with 0/50/100% tests; accrued but uncollected interest receives no terminal credit. Principal-release scenarios are assumptions, not proof of freed collateral.

Unusable GST compensation-cess credit ₹1.393 crore and old accrued interest are excluded from ordinary WC/cash. Recovery is separately tested, never double-counted with tax offsets. Other ordinary operating assets and dues remain in WC.

FY27–31 plus a fiscal stub to 19 October 2031 form the bridge. New capacity starts at 1% full-year utilization in base FY27, consistent with a late-year commissioning assumption rather than full-year output. Subsequent ramp, margin, maintenance capex and 8/10/12× multiples are analyst assumptions. No unverified peer multiple or project probability is assigned.

Bank borrowing is required finance, not a lender commitment. The explicit 20% equity alternative adds proceeds and shares together. Legacy and target rents are operating expenses in margins; no unreported capitalized lease liability is invented. Terminal equity excludes old investments, capital-advance assets and retained FD value except explicit recovery cases.
